transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, well, what brings me in is that I’m just... I'm exhausted. But in a way that sleep doesn’t really fix? I actually thought it was our bed at first, so we bought one of those memory foam mattress toppers a few weeks ago. The ones they always show on those commercials? My husband thought it was a waste of money, but I figured it was worth a try because, you know, they say you spend a third of your life in bed so you might as well be comfortable. 

But anyway, yeah, the sleep isn't fixing it. Just getting through a normal workday feels so much heavier than it should. I'm a manager, so I'm used to juggling a lot of moving parts and dealing with people's schedules, but lately... I don't know. Even just doing dinner at home afterward is a lot. Like, making a simple pasta dish just feels so draining. I was holding a jar of marinara sauce yesterday in the kitchen and just started thinking about the factory where they make it, and all those glass jars moving down a conveyor belt, and how loud that must be for the workers... I don't know. Everything just feels heavier than it should right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah, I suppose I have. Um... most days lately I wake up with this just... heavy, gray feeling. It's like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts, you know? Just opening my eyes and it's already there. 

Speaking of gray, we actually painted our bedroom this light gray color a few years ago. "Repose Gray," I think it was called. From Sherwin Williams. My sister swore it was the perfect neutral, but honestly, depending on the light, it sometimes looks a little purple? Especially in the late afternoon. She has it in her living room, but her house faces south, so she gets all that natural sunlight that warms it up. I always wanted a south-facing house, but when we were looking to buy, the market was just so crazy... we were outbid on three different places before we finally got this one. The inspection was a nightmare, too, the guy took like four hours. 

But anyway, I'm sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, feeling down. Yeah, just... that heavy feeling in the mornings.
Have you been getting less pleasure from things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I usually love painting. Watercolors, mostly. And I love wandering through museum exhibits on the weekends. We have this really nice little local art museum downtown that does these rotating exhibits every few months. The last one I went to was all about local landscapes from the 1920s, which was fascinating because you could see how much the riverfront has changed since then. They used to have all these old mills right on the water, and now it's all just luxury condos and coffee shops, you know? It's crazy how fast a city can change. My favorite coffee shop actually just closed down because the rent got too high, which is a shame because they had the best almond croissants. I tried making them at home once, but laminated dough is just... it's so much work. You have to keep chilling the butter block, and if your kitchen is too warm, it just melts everywhere and ruins the layers. 

But um... yeah, my painting supplies. I just leave them sitting there untouched lately. And the museum... I just can't make myself care enough to go right now. It just feels like too much effort to even think about it.
Did all of this start after a particular stressful event?

Stressful event? Um... no, not really? I mean, nothing major stands out. Work is always a little stressful just because I'm managing so many people, but it's just the usual stuff. Like, a couple of weeks ago corporate decided to switch our entire payroll software on a Tuesday, which makes absolutely zero sense. Why wouldn't you do a system migration on a Friday afternoon so IT has the whole weekend to fix the bugs? But no, Tuesday. And of course, everyone's login credentials got scrambled. 

I had this one employee, Dave, who got locked out of his account for three days. Dave is great, though, really nice guy. He actually brings in donuts every other Friday from this little bakery near his house. Not the big chain places, but a real mom-and-pop shop. They make these maple glazed ones with actual bacon on top. My husband thinks bacon on sweets is a crime against breakfast, but I think the salty-sweet combo is genius. It's like chocolate-covered pretzels, you know? We used to buy those in these huge tubs at Costco around the holidays... they come in that shiny red packaging. We'd always say we were going to give them away as gifts to the neighbors, but we usually just ended up eating them on the couch while watching movies. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh! Stressful events. Yeah, no, no big event or anything like that really happened to start all this.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, about a month, I think? Yeah, because before that, I was actually feeling really... really good. Like, unusually energized and driven, getting a million things done. I even reorganized the entire garage, which is saying something because we've been using it as a storage unit since we moved in. We had all these boxes of old college textbooks that we just couldn't bring ourselves to throw away. My husband was an engineering major, so his books are huge and weigh a ton. I don't know why they make textbooks so expensive, honestly. It's a complete racket. You pay two hundred dollars for a book, use it for one semester, and then the bookstore offers you twelve dollars to buy it back. It's insulting. 

When I was getting my bachelor's, I actually started buying international editions online to save money. They're exactly the same content, just printed in black and white on thinner paper. Sometimes the page numbers don't match up perfectly, but it's worth it when you're a broke college student living on ramen. Which, by the way, I can't even look at ramen anymore. There was this one place near campus that made authentic tonkotsu ramen, though, and that was different. The broth took them like twenty-four hours to make. 

But um, yeah, sorry. The low feeling. It's been about a month since I swung from feeling so energized down into this... this slump.
During that unusually energized period, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, actually. It was the weirdest thing. During that stretch, I was sleeping maybe four hours a night? And I'd still wake up just completely buzzing, ready to go. I'd be sending out work emails at 4:30 in the morning, sketching out ideas for this big corporate retreat we have coming up, or just completely reorganizing my kitchen cabinets. 

I actually bought all these clear acrylic bins for the pantry, you know, the ones you see on those home organization shows? They're so expensive, but they look so nice when you line up all your snacks in them. I color-coordinated the tea boxes and everything. I drink a lot of peppermint tea, especially in the winter. My grandmother used to grow her own mint in her backyard, and it would just take over the entire garden if she didn't keep it trimmed back. Mint is basically a weed, honestly. You have to plant it in a pot or it just spreads everywhere. She had this huge ceramic pot she kept it in, painted with these little blue birds. I think my sister ended up taking that pot when she passed away. My sister lives out in Arizona now, so I don't know how well mint grows out there in the desert. They have to water their lawns at like three in the morning just so it doesn't evaporate instantly. 

But um... yeah, sleep. Just about four hours a night, and I felt totally fine. Not tired at all.
During that unusually energized period, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Um, yeah, I did. Like, earlier in the month, I had this... this unusually charged, upbeat mood. I just felt brilliant, like every idea I had was gold. But then, almost in the same breath, I'd get so irritated, especially if my husband questioned any of my plans. Like, I decided we needed to repaint the guest room, and I went out and bought all this expensive paint. It was this beautiful shade called "Sea Glass." I saw it in a magazine at the dentist's office. 

My dentist is actually retiring next month, which is a huge bummer because he's the only one who doesn't lecture me about flossing. He just cleans my teeth and we talk about golf. I don't even play golf, but my dad was obsessed with it. He used to watch those tournaments on TV on Sunday afternoons, and the announcers always whisper so quietly. It's the most relaxing sound in the world, honestly. Better than those white noise machines. We bought one of those machines when my son was a baby because he wouldn't sleep through the neighbor's dog barking. That dog was a beagle, and they have that specific howl, you know? It's not a bark, it's like a baying sound. They use them for hunting, which makes sense, but not when you live in a cul-de-sac in the suburbs. 

But um, wait. Happy? Yeah, I felt really upbeat and brilliant, but then I'd snap at my husband if he didn't get on board with whatever I was doing right that second.
During that energized period, were you talking more than usual?

Yeah, actually, my husband mentioned that. He and a couple of my coworkers told me I was talking so fast and just... jumping in so much that they couldn't really get a word in. I didn't even realize I was doing it, honestly, I just felt like I had so much to say and it all needed to come out right then. 

It reminds me of this one coworker I used to have, Brenda. She worked in accounting, and she was a lovely person, really, but she would just talk at you for hours if you let her. You'd go into the breakroom to grab a coffee, and she'd corner you by the microwave to tell you all about her cat's dietary issues. Her cat had some kind of allergy to poultry, I think? Which is crazy because cats are basically built to eat birds. But she had to buy this special salmon-based food that cost like forty dollars a bag. 

I've never been a cat person, to be honest. We had a golden retriever growing up, and they're just so much friendlier. You walk in the door and they act like you've been gone for a year, even if you just went to check the mail. Our mail carrier, Gary, he's been delivering to our neighborhood for fifteen years. He always leaves a little dog treat in the mailbox for the neighbor's lab. It's so sweet. You don't see that kind of personal touch much anymore, especially with all the Amazon packages people get now. The delivery drivers are always rushing, throwing boxes on the porch and running back to their vans. 

But um, yeah... talking. I was definitely talking a lot more, and way faster than normal. They said it was hard to keep up with me.
During that energized period, did it cause serious problems at work, at home, or with other people?

Well, no, not serious problems. I mean, I was still showing up for work and doing what I needed to do around the house. It's just... I guess I've been a bit slower with making decisions lately, and maybe less reliable with family plans. I've also been pulling back from my art classes, which usually keep me pretty grounded and connected to people. 

I take this watercolor class at the community center on Thursday nights. The instructor, Marcus, he's incredibly talented. He did this whole series on local bridges that was actually featured in a gallery downtown last spring. Downtown has changed so much in the last five years, hasn't it? They tore down that old movie theater where my husband and I had our first date. It was a terrible date, honestly. We went to see some action movie he picked out, and the sound was so loud it gave me a migraine. I get migraines sometimes, especially when the barometric pressure drops. You can always tell when a storm is coming because the sky gets that weird, bruised purple color right before it breaks. 

My grandmother used to say that meant the angels were bowling. She had all these funny little sayings like that. She grew up on a farm in Ohio, so she was always paying attention to the weather. They grew corn mostly, and soybeans. I tried to grow tomatoes on my patio last summer, but the squirrels got to every single one before they even turned red. Squirrels are so bold these days. One actually came right up to my sliding glass door and just stared at me while I was drinking my coffee. I buy this hazelnut roast from a little shop near my office, it's so good. 

But um, anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, problems. Yeah, no, nothing serious. Just kind of dragging my feet on things and skipping my art stuff, but I'm still functioning fine.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, things get overwhelming sometimes, sure, but I'd never want to hurt myself or anything. There's still too much I want to do. Like, I actually just got off the waitlist for a plot at the community garden down the street. It only took two years! The woman who organizes it, Barbara, she runs a really tight ship. She actually used to be a principal at the middle school my son went to. 

Middle school is such a tough age, isn't it? All those hormones and the locker drama. My son lost his combination lock three times in one semester. We had to keep going to the local hardware store to buy new ones. The guy at the hardware store, Sal, he knows everything about everything. You can bring him a broken hinge from a cabinet from 1985 and he'll walk right to the exact bin in the back and hand you a replacement. Hardware stores always smell so specific, too, like... sawdust and fertilizer and cut keys. It reminds me of my grandfather's garage. He used to restore old radios. The big wooden ones, you know? They took up so much space, but the sound quality was incredibly warm. You just don't get that from Bluetooth speakers today. We bought a Bluetooth speaker for the patio last summer and it took my husband an hour just to get it to pair with his phone. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, hurting myself. No, definitely not. I haven't had any thoughts like that at all.
About how many days did that unusually energized period last?

Well, I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. It's hard to keep track of days when you're just go, go, go, you know? I'd say maybe a few days, maybe longer? Time is just a funny thing. Like, the other day, I was looking at the calendar and realized it's already been six months since we had our kitchen remodeled. Six months! It feels like just yesterday the contractors were here, tracking dust all over the hardwood floors. 

The main contractor, his name was Dave, he was always drinking these massive iced coffees from Dunkin' Donuts, even when it was freezing outside. I don't understand how people can drink iced coffee in the winter. It just makes you colder! My husband is the same way, though. He'll go out in a snowstorm in shorts and a t-shirt to grab the mail. We have this big oak tree near the mailbox, and the branches get so heavy with snow sometimes I worry they're going to snap. We had an arborist come out to look at it a couple of years ago. He said the tree was perfectly healthy, just old. It's probably been there since the house was built in the fifties. 

Houses from the fifties have such solid bones, you know? Not like the new construction they put up nowadays. They build these entire subdivisions in a matter of months, and they all look exactly the same. There's a new development going up near the highway, and every single house is painted that same shade of greige. It's so boring. I prefer a house with character. 

But um... wait, how long did the energized thing last? Yeah, I really couldn't give you an exact number of days. I just didn't really pay attention to the timeline.
Did that unusually energized period last at least four days in a row?

Well, like I said, I'm really not sure about the exact number of days. I mean, it could have been four days, maybe? It's just so hard to say for sure when you're caught up in it. It's like trying to remember how long a dream lasted, you know? 

Speaking of dreams, I had the weirdest one last night. I was back in college, trying to find my way to a final exam for a class I hadn't attended all semester. The campus was completely different, though. It looked more like a giant shopping mall, with escalators going in every direction. I used to love going to the mall when I was a teenager. We had this big one near my hometown with a massive food court. The Orange Julius stand was my absolute favorite. Do they even make Orange Julius anymore? I feel like I haven't seen one in years. 

It's funny how things just disappear like that, isn't it? Like payphones. You used to see payphones everywhere, and now they're practically extinct. I remember using a payphone to call my mom when my car broke down on the side of the highway right after I got my license. I was so panicked, and I had to dig through my purse for what felt like hours just to find a quarter. Quarters used to buy so much more back then. Now you can't even get a gumball for a quarter. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, four days. Yeah, I honestly couldn't tell you if it was exactly four days in a row. It's all just a blur, really.
During that unusually energized time, did you do anything impulsive or risky that was out of character for you?

No, I wouldn't say I did anything risky or impulsive. I mean, I'm a manager, so I'm used to making decisions and being responsible. You have to be, when you're managing a team. My team at work, they're mostly younger, right out of college. It's funny, they all use these different apps for everything now. Like, nobody just emails anymore, it's all Slack messages and shared documents. 

I remember when I first started working, we actually had physical interoffice mail envelopes. The ones with the little string you wrap around the circles? They were always covered in crossing-out names from the people who used them before. It was almost like a history of the company right there on the envelope. My first boss, Mr. Henderson, he insisted on printing out every single email and putting it in a physical file folder. He had these massive filing cabinets that took up half his office. 

Filing cabinets are so heavy, too. We tried to move one when we rearranged the home office last spring, and it scratched the floor. My husband was so mad, he spent the entire weekend trying to buff it out with this special wax he ordered online. He buys so much stuff online now. The delivery guys know our dog by name. Buster, he's a golden retriever mix. He barks at the mailman, but he absolutely loves the UPS driver because he always has treats. 

But um... what did you ask? Oh, right, doing risky things. No, no. I didn't do anything like that. I'm pretty careful, usually.
Did that unusually energized, upbeat period last a full four days or more?

Well, yeah, it definitely lasted more than four days. It was actually for a couple of weeks, now that I really think about it. I just had so much energy, like I was bouncing between all my work projects, and then I'd jump right into these art committee calls, and then I'd be up organizing the house... I just couldn't slow down. 

Speaking of the art committee, we're trying to plan this silent auction for the spring, and it is just a nightmare trying to get everyone on the same page. We have this one woman, Brenda, who insists we need to have it at the botanical gardens, but they charge an absolute fortune for event space. Have you ever tried to rent a venue lately? The prices are astronomical. And they nickel and dime you for everything. Oh, you want chairs? That's an extra fee. You want a microphone? Extra fee. 

My niece got married last year, and they ended up doing it in her fiancé's parents' backyard just to save money. It was actually beautiful, though. They strung up all these fairy lights in the trees, and they had this amazing taco truck instead of a formal sit-down dinner. I love a good taco truck. There's one that parks near my office on Tuesdays, and they make these incredible al pastor tacos with fresh pineapple. Pineapple on tacos sounds weird, but it totally works. Kind of like pineapple on pizza, which I know is controversial. My husband hates it, but I think the sweet and salty combination is perfect. 

But um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the energy. Yeah, it was a solid couple of weeks of just going and going like that.
During that unusually energized period, were you ever hospitalized because of it?

No, I wasn't hospitalized or anything like that. I mean, I didn't need to be, I was just getting a lot done. Hospitals always make me so anxious anyway. The smell of them, you know? It's that awful mix of bleach and rubbing alcohol and... I don't know, institutional food? 

My grandmother was in the hospital for a few weeks when I was a teenager, and I hated going to visit her. Not because I didn't love her, but just the environment. She had this roommate who watched game shows at maximum volume all day long. *The Price is Right*, *Wheel of Fortune*, *Jeopardy!*... it was just a constant stream of bells and buzzers. I used to love watching *Jeopardy!* with my dad, though. He knew the answer to almost everything. He was a history teacher, so any category about presidents or wars, he'd have the answer before Alex Trebek even finished reading the clue. 

I think being a teacher would be so exhausting. Just standing up in front of teenagers all day, trying to get them to care about the War of 1812. Kids today just seem so distracted, with their phones and TikTok and everything. My neighbor's daughter is 14, and she was telling me she wants to be an "influencer" when she grows up. Not a doctor or a lawyer, an influencer. It just blows my mind how much the world has changed since I was that age. We just wanted to hang out at the roller rink and listen to Madonna. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, hospitals. Yeah, no, I never went to the hospital for any of that energy stuff. I just rode it out at home and at work.
Has this low, heavy mood been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah, it’s definitely been at least two weeks. It feels like it’s been forever, honestly. Most days lately, I just wake up with this heavy, gray feeling... it's like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts. I just lie there in bed looking at the ceiling fan. 

We actually had to replace that ceiling fan last month because it started making this awful clicking noise on the medium setting. Click, click, click, all night long. My husband tried to fix it himself, but you know how that goes. He watched three different YouTube tutorials and ended up having to go to Home Depot twice on a Sunday. I don't know why people think they can just learn electrical work from a ten-minute video. 

It's like when my brother-in-law tried to build his own deck. He bought all the lumber and then it just sat in his driveway for six months under a blue tarp. The homeowner's association finally sent them a warning letter. HOAs are so strict about that kind of thing. Our HOA president, Susan, she actually walks around the neighborhood with a little clipboard checking if everyone's grass is cut to the right height. It's a bit much, honestly. She even complained about the color of the mulch we put in our front flowerbeds last spring. Who cares about mulch? It's literally just ground-up wood. 

But um... wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the heavy feeling in the mornings. Yeah, it's been pretty much every day, all day, for a couple of weeks now. Just this constant gray cloud.
Has this low mood made it hard for you to function at work or at home?

Well, I’m still showing up for work and doing my home responsibilities, so I haven't completely stopped functioning or anything. But I’ve definitely been a lot slower with my decisions at work. Being a manager, you know, people are always waiting on me to approve things, like this new payroll software we're trying to roll out. It is a complete disaster. They promised us it would streamline everything, but the interface is just so clunky. It honestly reminds me of those old boxy computers we used to have back in college in the nineties. 

My freshman year roommate had this giant desktop that sounded like a jet engine taking off every time she booted it up. She was a graphic design major, so she needed all this processing power. She actually ended up designing my wedding invitations a few years later, which was so sweet of her. We used this really heavy, beautiful cardstock with a deckled edge. Have you ever tried to mail something with a deckled edge, though? The post office is so incredibly particular about odd-sized or textured envelopes. They hit you with a surcharge for every little thing. It's like, I just want to send a piece of paper in the mail, why does it need to be a federal ordeal? My aunt actually works for the post office in Ohio, and she says the automated sorting machines just chew up anything that isn't perfectly flat and standard. 

But um... wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, functioning. Yeah, so work is just taking me longer because my brain feels slow. And then outside of work, I've been a lot less reliable with family plans. I just end up canceling on people at the last minute. I’ve also been way more withdrawn from my art activities, which is a shame because those usually keep me connected to everyone. I just don't have it in me right now.
Since this low period started, have you noticed your thoughts moving unusually fast or jumping from one idea to another?

Yeah, it's exactly like that. It honestly feels like my mind has way too many tabs open at once. I'll have ideas for work, stuff for my cultural group, and our whole household schedule just all racing through together at the same time. 

Speaking of tabs, I actually crashed my work computer on Tuesday because I had too many browser windows open trying to cross-reference some reports. Our IT guy, Kevin, had to come down and reset the whole system. Kevin is always so condescending about that stuff. He sighs really loudly while he types, like you're personally ruining his day. And he always wears these novelty ties—like, one day it was rubber chickens, another day it was little golf clubs. I don't even know where you buy ties like that anymore. Do they still have those joke shops in the mall? 

Malls are just so depressing these days anyway. I went to the one near us last month to look for a birthday gift for my sister, and half the stores were just boarded up or replaced by those weird pop-up places selling cell phone cases. I ended up just getting her a gift card to a nice restaurant, which always feels like a bit of a cop-out, but she loves going out to eat. She and her husband go to this Italian place every anniversary where they toss the hot pasta right in front of you in a giant, hollowed-out wheel of parmesan cheese. It looks amazing, but I'm lactose intolerant, so that would completely ruin my week. I have to buy that expensive oat milk now, and even that has a weird aftertaste if you put it in coffee. 

But um... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my thoughts. Yeah, they just go really fast, like I was saying. Just racing with all the work and household stuff at once.
Lately, have you been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Well, yeah, actually. My staff has definitely noticed. They've pointed out that I’m slower to answer questions in meetings lately. It's like there’s this long pause before I can even get my thoughts and words moving to respond to them. 

Which is really frustrating because we have these weekly check-in meetings on Thursday mornings, and they usually expect me to just fire off answers. We do them in the big conference room on the second floor, the one with the huge glass windows. It gets so incredibly hot in there because the morning sun just beats right through the glass, and the building's AC can never keep up. I actually brought in a little desk fan to plug in during those meetings, but then someone complained that the whirring noise was distracting. 

People are so sensitive to noise in offices now since everyone got used to working from home. My neighbor's dog barks constantly while I'm trying to work from home on Fridays. It's a Goldendoodle, and I swear it just barks at the wind. They're supposed to be these smart, trainable dogs, but this one is completely out of control. I read an article that said those doodle mixes are actually really prone to anxiety because of the poodle genetics. My cousin used to breed poodles, standard ones, back in the eighties. They are so high maintenance with the grooming. You have to take them in every six weeks or they get matted down to the skin. I could never deal with a pet that requires more hair care than I do. I barely have time to get my own roots touched up these days. My stylist moved to a salon all the way across town, so now it's a whole production just to get a trim. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, moving slow. Yeah, the staff said I'm just taking a lot longer to get my words out in those meetings.
During this low period, have you heard or seen things that other people couldn’t, or had beliefs that others said weren’t true?

No, no, nothing like that. I haven't been seeing things or hearing voices or anything. I know what's real and what isn't. 

Speaking of what's real, though, there's this new reality show my husband has been watching. It is so clearly scripted, I don't know how he can stand it. They put all these strangers on an island and pretend they're surviving, but you can clearly see they have perfectly styled hair and makeup in half the shots. I mean, who brings a curling iron to a deserted island? And where would you even plug it in? My husband insists it's authentic, but he's always been a little gullible with television. He used to watch those ghost hunting shows and genuinely believe every little creak in the floorboards was a poltergeist. 

We actually had an old house when we first got married, built in like 1920, and it creaked all the time. The plumbing was terrible, too. We had to replace all the pipes in the basement because they were galvanized steel and completely corroded on the inside. The plumber who came out charged us an absolute fortune. He drove this huge, custom-painted van with a giant wrench on the side. I remember thinking, "Well, I'm definitely paying for that paint job." It took them three days to finish the work, and the water was shut off the whole time. We had to shower at the gym, which was so inconvenient because the gym showers always smell faintly of mildew and cheap eucalyptus body wash. I actually canceled my gym membership last year because they raised the monthly fee by thirty dollars and didn't even upgrade the equipment. 

But um... wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, seeing things. No, no hallucinations or weird beliefs or anything like that. Just the low mood and feeling slow.

They make these maple glazed ones with actual bacon on top. My husband thinks bacon on sweets is a crime against breakfast, but I think the salty-sweet combo is genius. It's like chocolate-covered pretzels, you know? We used to buy those in these huge tubs at Costco around the holidays... they come in that shiny red packaging. Sometimes the page numbers don't match up perfectly, but it's worth it when you're a broke college student living on ramen. Which, by the way, I can't even look at ramen anymore. There was this one place near campus that made authentic tonkotsu ramen, though, and that was different. The broth took them like twenty-four hours to make.

patient.answer:
Yeah, actually. It was the weirdest thing. During that stretch, I was sleeping maybe four hours a night? And I'd still wake up just completely buzzing, ready to go. I'd be sending out work emails at 4:30 in the morning, sketching out ideas for this big corporate retreat we have coming up, or just completely reorganizing my kitchen cabinets. 

I actually bought all these clear acrylic bins for the pantry, you know, the ones you see on those home organization shows? They're so expensive, but they look so nice when you line up all your snacks in them. I color-coordinated the tea boxes and everything. I drink a lot of peppermint tea, especially in the winter. My grandmother used to grow her own mint in her backyard, and it would just take over the entire garden if she didn't keep it trimmed back. Mint is basically a weed, honestly. You have to plant it in a pot or it just spreads everywhere. She had this huge ceramic pot she kept it in, painted with these little blue birds. I think my sister ended up taking that pot when she passed away. My sister lives out in Arizona now, so I don't know how well mint grows out there in the desert. They have to water their lawns at like three in the morning just so it doesn't evaporate instantly. 

But um... yeah, sleep. Just about four hours a night, and I felt totally fine. Not tired at all.

patient.answer:
Um, yeah, I did. Like, earlier in the month, I had this... this unusually charged, upbeat mood. I just felt brilliant, like every idea I had was gold. But then, almost in the same breath, I'd get so irritated, especially if my husband questioned any of my plans. Like, I decided we needed to repaint the guest room, and I went out and bought all this expensive paint. It was this beautiful shade called "Sea Glass." I saw it in a magazine at the dentist's office. 

My dentist is actually retiring next month, which is a huge bummer because he's the only one who doesn't lecture me about flossing. He just cleans my teeth and we talk about golf. I don't even play golf, but my dad was obsessed with it. He used to watch those tournaments on TV on Sunday afternoons, and the announcers always whisper so quietly. It's the most relaxing sound in the world, honestly. Better than those white noise machines. We bought one of those machines when my son was a baby because he wouldn't sleep through the neighbor's dog barking. That dog was a beagle, and they have that specific howl, you know? It's not a bark, it's like a baying sound. They use them for hunting, which makes sense, but not when you live in a cul-de-sac in the suburbs. 

But um, wait. Happy? Yeah, I felt really upbeat and brilliant, but then I'd snap at my husband if he didn't get on board with whatever I was doing right that second.

Yeah, actually, my husband mentioned that. He and a couple of my coworkers told me I was talking so fast and just... jumping in so much that they couldn't really get a word in. I didn't even realize I was doing it, honestly, I just felt like I had so much to say and it all needed to come out right then. 

It reminds me of this one coworker I used to have, Brenda. She worked in accounting, and she was a lovely person, really, but she would just talk at you for hours if you let her. You'd go into the breakroom to grab a coffee, and she'd corner you by the microwave to tell you all about her cat's dietary issues. Her cat had some kind of allergy to poultry, I think? Which is crazy because cats are basically built to eat birds. But she had to buy this special salmon-based food that cost like forty dollars a bag. 

I've never been a cat person, to be honest. We had a golden retriever growing up, and they're just so much friendlier. You walk in the door and they act like you've been gone for a year, even if you just went to check the mail. Our mail carrier, Gary, he's been delivering to our neighborhood for fifteen years. He always leaves a little dog treat in the mailbox for the neighbor's lab. It's so sweet. You don't see that kind of personal touch much anymore, especially with all the Amazon packages people get now. The delivery drivers are always rushing, throwing boxes on the porch and running back to their vans. 

But um, yeah... talking. I was definitely talking a lot more, and way faster than normal. They said it was hard to keep up with me.

Well, no, not serious problems. I mean, I was still showing up for work and doing what I needed to do around the house. It's just... I take this watercolor class at the community center on Thursday nights. The instructor, Marcus, he's incredibly talented. He did this whole series on local bridges that was actually featured in a gallery downtown last spring. Downtown has changed so much in the last five years, hasn't it? They tore down that old movie theater where my husband and I had our first date. It was a terrible date, honestly. We went to see some action movie he picked out, and the sound was so loud it gave me a migraine. I get migraines sometimes, especially when the barometric pressure drops. You can always tell when a storm is coming because the sky gets that weird, bruised purple color right before it breaks. 

My grandmother used to say that meant the angels were bowling. She had all these funny little sayings like that. She grew up on a farm in Ohio, so she was always paying attention to the weather. They grew corn mostly, and soybeans. I tried to grow tomatoes on my patio last summer, but the squirrels got to every single one before they even turned red. Squirrels are so bold these days. One actually came right up to my sliding glass door and just stared at me while I was drinking my coffee. I buy this hazelnut roast from a little shop near my office, it's so good. 

But um, anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, problems. Yeah, no, nothing serious. Just kind of dragging my feet on things and skipping my art stuff, but I'm still functioning fine.

She actually used to be a principal at the middle school my son went to. 

Middle school is such a tough age, isn't it? All those hormones and the locker drama. My son lost his combination lock three times in one semester. We had to keep going to the local hardware store to buy new ones. The guy at the hardware store, Sal, he knows everything about everything. You can bring him a broken hinge from a cabinet from 1985 and he'll walk right to the exact bin in the back and hand you a replacement. Hardware stores always smell so specific, too, like... sawdust and fertilizer and cut keys. It reminds me of my grandfather's garage. He used to restore old radios. The big wooden ones, you know? They took up so much space, but the sound quality was incredibly warm. You just don't get that from Bluetooth speakers today. We bought a Bluetooth speaker for the patio last summer and it took my husband an hour just to get it to pair with his phone. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, hurting myself. No, definitely not. I haven't had any thoughts like that at all.

Well, I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. It's hard to keep track of days when you're just go, go, go, you know? I'd say maybe a few days, maybe longer? Time is just a funny thing. Like, the other day, I was looking at the calendar and realized it's already been six months since we had our kitchen remodeled. Six months! It feels like just yesterday the contractors were here, tracking dust all over the hardwood floors. 

The main contractor, his name was Dave, he was always drinking these massive iced coffees from Dunkin' Donuts, even when it was freezing outside. I don't understand how people can drink iced coffee in the winter. It just makes you colder! My husband is the same way, though. He'll go out in a snowstorm in shorts and a t-shirt to grab the mail. We have this big oak tree near the mailbox, and the branches get so heavy with snow sometimes I worry they're going to snap. We had an arborist come out to look at it a couple of years ago. He said the tree was perfectly healthy, just old. It's probably been there since the house was built in the fifties. 

Houses from the fifties have such solid bones, you know? Not like the new construction they put up nowadays. They build these entire subdivisions in a matter of months, and they all look exactly the same. There's a new development going up near the highway, and every single house is painted that same shade of greige. It's so boring. I prefer a house with character. 

But um... wait, how long did the energized thing last? Yeah, I really couldn't give you an exact number of days. I just didn't really pay attention to the timeline.

Well, like I said, I'm really not sure about the exact number of days. I mean, it could have been four days, maybe? It's just so hard to say for sure when you're caught up in it. It's like trying to remember how long a dream lasted, you know? 

Speaking of dreams, I had the weirdest one last night. I was back in college, trying to find my way to a final exam for a class I hadn't attended all semester. The campus was completely different, though. It looked more like a giant shopping mall, with escalators going in every direction. I used to love going to the mall when I was a teenager. We had this big one near my hometown with a massive food court. The Orange Julius stand was my absolute favorite. Do they even make Orange Julius anymore? I feel like I haven't seen one in years. 

It's funny how things just disappear like that, isn't it? Like payphones. You used to see payphones everywhere, and now they're practically extinct. I remember using a payphone to call my mom when my car broke down on the side of the highway right after I got my license. I was so panicked, and I had to dig through my purse for what felt like hours just to find a quarter. Quarters used to buy so much more back then. Now you can't even get a gumball for a quarter. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, four days. Yeah, I honestly couldn't tell you if it was exactly four days in a row. It's all just a blur, really.

No, I wouldn't say I did anything risky or impulsive. I mean, I'm a manager, so I'm used to making decisions and being responsible. You have to be, when you're managing a team. My team at work, they're mostly younger, right out of college. It's funny, they all use these different apps for everything now. Like, nobody just emails anymore, it's all Slack messages and shared documents. 

I remember when I first started working, we actually had physical interoffice mail envelopes. The ones with the little string you wrap around the circles? They were always covered in crossing-out names from the people who used them before. It was almost like a history of the company right there on the envelope. My first boss, Mr. Henderson, he insisted on printing out every single email and putting it in a physical file folder. He had these massive filing cabinets that took up half his office. 

Filing cabinets are so heavy, too. We tried to move one when we rearranged the home office last spring, and it scratched the floor. My husband was so mad, he spent the entire weekend trying to buff it out with this special wax he ordered online. He buys so much stuff online now. The delivery guys know our dog by name. Buster, he's a golden retriever mix. He barks at the mailman, but he absolutely loves the UPS driver because he always has treats. 

But um... what did you ask? Oh, right, doing risky things. No, no. I didn't do anything like that. I'm pretty careful, usually.

Well, yeah, it definitely lasted more than four days. It was actually for a couple of weeks, now that I really think about it. Speaking of the art committee, we're trying to plan this silent auction for the spring, and it is just a nightmare trying to get everyone on the same page. We have this one woman, Brenda, who insists we need to have it at the botanical gardens, but they charge an absolute fortune for event space. Have you ever tried to rent a venue lately? The prices are astronomical. And they nickel and dime you for everything. Oh, you want chairs? That's an extra fee. You want a microphone? Extra fee. 

My niece got married last year, and they ended up doing it in her fiancé's parents' backyard just to save money. It was actually beautiful, though. They strung up all these fairy lights in the trees, and they had this amazing taco truck instead of a formal sit-down dinner. I love a good taco truck. There's one that parks near my office on Tuesdays, and they make these incredible al pastor tacos with fresh pineapple. Pineapple on tacos sounds weird, but it totally works. Kind of like pineapple on pizza, which I know is controversial. My husband hates it, but I think the sweet and salty combination is perfect. 

But um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the energy. Yeah, it was a solid couple of weeks of just going and going like that.

No, I wasn't hospitalized or anything like that. I mean, I didn't need to be, I was just getting a lot done. Hospitals always make me so anxious anyway. The smell of them, you know? It's that awful mix of bleach and rubbing alcohol and... I don't know, institutional food? 

My grandmother was in the hospital for a few weeks when I was a teenager, and I hated going to visit her. Not because I didn't love her, but just the environment. She had this roommate who watched game shows at maximum volume all day long. *The Price is Right*, *Wheel of Fortune*, *Jeopardy!*... it was just a constant stream of bells and buzzers. I used to love watching *Jeopardy!* with my dad, though. He knew the answer to almost everything. He was a history teacher, so any category about presidents or wars, he'd have the answer before Alex Trebek even finished reading the clue. 

I think being a teacher would be so exhausting. Just standing up in front of teenagers all day, trying to get them to care about the War of 1812. Kids today just seem so distracted, with their phones and TikTok and everything. My neighbor's daughter is 14, and she was telling me she wants to be an "influencer" when she grows up. Not a doctor or a lawyer, an influencer. It just blows my mind how much the world has changed since I was that age. We just wanted to hang out at the roller rink and listen to Madonna. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, hospitals. Yeah, no, I never went to the hospital for any of that energy stuff. I just rode it out at home and at work.

My husband tried to fix it himself, but you know how that goes. He watched three different YouTube tutorials and ended up having to go to Home Depot twice on a Sunday. I don't know why people think they can just learn electrical work from a ten-minute video. 

It's like when my brother-in-law tried to build his own deck. He bought all the lumber and then it just sat in his driveway for six months under a blue tarp. The homeowner's association finally sent them a warning letter. HOAs are so strict about that kind of thing. Our HOA president, Susan, she actually walks around the neighborhood with a little clipboard checking if everyone's grass is cut to the right height. It's a bit much, honestly. She even complained about the color of the mulch we put in our front flowerbeds last spring. Who cares about mulch? It's literally just ground-up wood. 

But um... wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the heavy feeling in the mornings. Yeah, it's been pretty much every day, all day, for a couple of weeks now. Just this constant gray cloud.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode includes significant impairment in functioning, which would support bipolar II disorder rather than a milder depressive state or nonspecific fatigue.
doctor.question: Has this low mood made it hard for you to function at work or at home?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m still showing up for work and home responsibilities, but I’ve been slower with decisions, less reliable with family plans, and more withdrawn from the art activities that usually keep me connected.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the low mood has impacted the patient's ability to function at work or at home, which directly matches the functional impairment item.

patient.answer:
Well, I’m still showing up for work and doing my home responsibilities, so I haven't completely stopped functioning or anything. But I’ve definitely been a lot slower with my decisions at work. Being a manager, you know, people are always waiting on me to approve things, like this new payroll software we're trying to roll out. It is a complete disaster. They promised us it would streamline everything, but the interface is just so clunky. It honestly reminds me of those old boxy computers we used to have back in college in the nineties. 

My freshman year roommate had this giant desktop that sounded like a jet engine taking off every time she booted it up. She was a graphic design major, so she needed all this processing power. She actually ended up designing my wedding invitations a few years later, which was so sweet of her. We used this really heavy, beautiful cardstock with a deckled edge. Have you ever tried to mail something with a deckled edge, though? The post office is so incredibly particular about odd-sized or textured envelopes. They hit you with a surcharge for every little thing. It's like, I just want to send a piece of paper in the mail, why does it need to be a federal ordeal? My aunt actually works for the post office in Ohio, and she says the automated sorting machines just chew up anything that isn't perfectly flat and standard. 

But um... wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, functioning. Yeah, so work is just taking me longer because my brain feels slow. And then outside of work, I've been a lot less reliable with family plans. I just end up canceling on people at the last minute. I’ve also been way more withdrawn from my art activities, which is a shame because those usually keep me connected to everyone. I just don't have it in me right now.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive period includes a core manic-depressive symptom pattern strongly supporting bipolar II disorder rather than unipolar depression or generalized anxiety.
doctor.question: Since this low period started, have you noticed your thoughts moving unusually fast or jumping from one idea to another?

target_item.name: Racing_Thoughts
target_item.manifestation: My mind felt like it had too many tabs open at once, with ideas for work, the cultural group, and our household schedule all racing through together.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient has noticed thoughts moving unusually fast or jumping from one idea to another, which directly corresponds to Racing Thoughts (S038).

patient.answer:
Yeah, it's exactly like that. It honestly feels like my mind has way too many tabs open at once. I'll have ideas for work, stuff for my cultural group, and our whole household schedule just all racing through together at the same time. 

Speaking of tabs, I actually crashed my work computer on Tuesday because I had too many browser windows open trying to cross-reference some reports. Our IT guy, Kevin, had to come down and reset the whole system. Kevin is always so condescending about that stuff. He sighs really loudly while he types, like you're personally ruining his day. And he always wears these novelty ties—like, one day it was rubber chickens, another day it was little golf clubs. I don't even know where you buy ties like that anymore. Do they still have those joke shops in the mall? 

Malls are just so depressing these days anyway. I went to the one near us last month to look for a birthday gift for my sister, and half the stores were just boarded up or replaced by those weird pop-up places selling cell phone cases. I ended up just getting her a gift card to a nice restaurant, which always feels like a bit of a cop-out, but she loves going out to eat. She and her husband go to this Italian place every anniversary where they toss the hot pasta right in front of you in a giant, hollowed-out wheel of parmesan cheese. It looks amazing, but I'm lactose intolerant, so that would completely ruin my week. I have to buy that expensive oat milk now, and even that has a weird aftertaste if you put it in coffee. 

But um... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my thoughts. Yeah, they just go really fast, like I was saying. Just racing with all the work and household stuff at once.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the current depressive episode includes psychomotor retardation, a key symptom that helps distinguish a major depressive episode from nonspecific fatigue or generalized anxiety and supports bipolar II disorder if present after a hypomanic period.
doctor.question: Lately, have you been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: My staff has noticed I’m slower to answer questions in meetings, like there’s a pause before I can get my thoughts and words moving.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have been moving or speaking more slowly than usual, which relates to observable decreases in psychomotor activity.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, actually. My staff has definitely noticed. They've pointed out that I’m slower to answer questions in meetings lately. It's like there’s this long pause before I can even get my thoughts and words moving to respond to them. 

Which is really frustrating because we have these weekly check-in meetings on Thursday mornings, and they usually expect me to just fire off answers. We do them in the big conference room on the second floor, the one with the huge glass windows. It gets so incredibly hot in there because the morning sun just beats right through the glass, and the building's AC can never keep up. I actually brought in a little desk fan to plug in during those meetings, but then someone complained that the whirring noise was distracting. 

People are so sensitive to noise in offices now since everyone got used to working from home. My neighbor's dog barks constantly while I'm trying to work from home on Fridays. It's a Goldendoodle, and I swear it just barks at the wind. They're supposed to be these smart, trainable dogs, but this one is completely out of control. I read an article that said those doodle mixes are actually really prone to anxiety because of the poodle genetics. My cousin used to breed poodles, standard ones, back in the eighties. They are so high maintenance with the grooming. You have to take them in every six weeks or they get matted down to the skin. I could never deal with a pet that requires more hair care than I do. I barely have time to get my own roots touched up these days. My stylist moved to a salon all the way across town, so now it's a whole production just to get a trim. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, moving slow. Yeah, the staff said I'm just taking a lot longer to get my words out in those meetings.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the current depressive episode includes psychotic features, which would meaningfully affect diagnosis/specification and management.
doctor.question: During this low period, have you heard or seen things that other people couldn’t, or had beliefs that others said weren’t true?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about hallucinations or delusions (psychotic symptoms), which are not present in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, no, nothing like that. I haven't been seeing things or hearing voices or anything. I know what's real and what isn't. 

Speaking of what's real, though, there's this new reality show my husband has been watching. It is so clearly scripted, I don't know how he can stand it. They put all these strangers on an island and pretend they're surviving, but you can clearly see they have perfectly styled hair and makeup in half the shots. I mean, who brings a curling iron to a deserted island? And where would you even plug it in? My husband insists it's authentic, but he's always been a little gullible with television. He used to watch those ghost hunting shows and genuinely believe every little creak in the floorboards was a poltergeist. 

We actually had an old house when we first got married, built in like 1920, and it creaked all the time. The plumbing was terrible, too. We had to replace all the pipes in the basement because they were galvanized steel and completely corroded on the inside. The plumber who came out charged us an absolute fortune. He drove this huge, custom-painted van with a giant wrench on the side. I remember thinking, "Well, I'm definitely paying for that paint job." It took them three days to finish the work, and the water was shut off the whole time. We had to shower at the gym, which was so inconvenient because the gym showers always smell faintly of mildew and cheap eucalyptus body wash. I actually canceled my gym membership last year because they raised the monthly fee by thirty dollars and didn't even upgrade the equipment. 

But um... wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, seeing things. No, no hallucinations or weird beliefs or anything like that. Just the low mood and feeling slow.

inference.note: History now clearly supports a major depressive episode following a distinct hypomanic episode lasting a couple of weeks, with decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, increased talkativeness, racing thoughts, and no hospitalization/psychosis or marked impairment; this rules against unipolar F32.9/F33.9 and makes F41.1/R53.83 secondary rather than primary.

opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a current major depressive episode with at least 2 weeks of depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, psychomotor slowing, impaired concentration/decision-making, and functional decline, preceded by a distinct hypomanic period lasting a couple of weeks with decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, pressured speech, and racing thoughts. There was no hospitalization, no psychosis, and no clear severe impairment during the elevated period, supporting bipolar II disorder rather than bipolar I.
